title: monitoring agents / Manage OTel configuration for your organization
content: ## Manage OTel configuration for your organization Enterprises can mandate OTel export configuration centrally through {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} enterprise-managed settings, without each developer setting `OTEL_*` environment variables. Managed telemetry configuration applies to both the Copilot Chat extension and the Agent Host process. In addition to collector export, Copilot Agent Host sessions support a managed file destination. For delivery methods, configuration fields, client support, and precedence, see [`telemetry` in the enterprise-managed settings reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings#telemetry). For the behavior specific to {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}, see [Apply managed telemetry in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#apply-managed-telemetry-in-vs-code). For Local harness sessions, {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} automatically tries once per editor session to restart the extension hosts when a managed OTel configuration that enables export arrives after Copilot Chat starts. The restart can interrupt other extensions. If the automatic restart can't complete, or for later policy changes, select **Reload Window** when prompted. > [!NOTE] > When a managed telemetry value is configured, it overrides user settings. Managed identity capture also overrides `COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_IDENTITY`, and managed resource attributes override `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`. Remove other conflicting OTel environment variables from managed devices to ensure that the enterprise configuration takes effect in the Copilot Chat extension. ### Export managed telemetry to a file Starting with {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} 1.143, administrators can set `telemetry.filePath` to save Copilot Agent Host telemetry as JSON Lines (JSONL), without running an OTLP collector or requiring developers to opt in through personal OTel settings. This managed destination is separate from the Copilot Chat extension's [file exporter](#other-exporter-examples). For a local Agent Host, add the following telemetry block to the device-wide `managed-settings.json` file, not your editor settings JSON: | Platform | Managed settings file | |---|---| | macOS | `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json` | | Linux | `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` | | Windows | `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json` | ```json { "telemetry": { "filePath": "~/copilot-telemetry/copilot-otel.jsonl", "captureContent": false, "capture": { "identity": false } } } ``` Choose an absolute or home-relative output path that the Agent Host can write to. Paths refer to the machine that exports the telemetry. The `~/` prefix expands to that machine's user home directory. Environment-variable references such as `$HOME` or `%USERPROFILE%` in `filePath` are not expanded and are rejected. Setting `filePath` enables Agent Host OTel export without `enabled: true`. An explicit managed `telemetry.enabled: false` takes precedence and turns off export. After {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} resolves a managed telemetry change, it restarts the local Agent Host automatically. Start a new Copilot Agent Host session and send a prompt, then check the destination file for spans such as `invoke_agent` and `vscode.agent_host.session`. The exporter creates missing parent directories and appends one span per line. If it cannot resolve the path or write to the file, the Agent Host logs an error without blocking chat. It does not fall back to a collector. Apply your organization's access and retention controls to the exported files. > [!IMPORTANT] > A managed `filePath` takes precedence over collector configuration. While it is configured, Agent Host telemetry goes to the file instead of the collector, and [dynamic headers](#configure-dynamic-headers) do not apply. Include the file configuration in the [highest-precedence managed telemetry block](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#apply-managed-telemetry-in-vs-code). To remove the managed file destination, remove `telemetry.filePath` from the effective managed configuration. After the change is applied, another configured collector or personal Agent Host exporter can become effective again. Removing `filePath` stops all export only when no other exporter is configured. To turn off Agent Host OTel export through managed settings, set `telemetry.enabled` to `false`. ### Configure dynamic headers Starting with {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} 1.143, administrators can configure `telemetry.headersProvider` for Copilot Agent Host sessions to generate and refresh HTTP headers for OTLP export. The Agent Host runs a helper executable to obtain header values, so developers don't need to update them manually. Use these headers to supply collector-specific metadata, route telemetry, or authenticate with the collector. Configure the provider through {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} enterprise-managed settings, not your editor settings JSON. For example, deploy the following telemetry block in `managed-settings.json`: ```json { "telemetry": { "enabled": true, "endpoint": "https://:4318", "protocol": "http/protobuf", "captureContent": false, "capture": { "identity": false }, "headers": { "x-organization": "" }, "headersProvider": { "path": "", "args": [], "refreshIntervalMs": 1740000 } } } ``` Replace the endpoint, organization ID, and helper path with your deployment values. Install the helper and its dependencies on the machine where the Agent Host runs. For remote sessions, the executable and paths must exist on the remote host. The helper runs from the execution host's home directory, with the arguments in `args` passed without shell evaluation. It must finish within 30 seconds and write a JSON object with string values to standard output: ```json { "x-team": "platform", "x-environment": "production" } ``` The helper can also return an `Authorization` header when the collector requires authentication. The provider refreshes headers every 29 minutes by default. Set `refreshIntervalMs` to match how often your header values need to be refreshed. Returning `{}` clears dynamic headers. If a refresh fails, exports that require dynamic headers are blocked until the provider refreshes successfully. Headers returned by the provider take precedence over managed static `telemetry.headers` values with the same name. Nonconflicting static headers remain in the request. Managed headers also take precedence over user-provided headers. The provider requires an `endpoint` in the same telemetry block and supports HTTP OTLP export with `http/protobuf` or `http/json`, not gRPC. Managed export does not require developers to opt in through personal OTel settings. Higher-precedence managed sources replace the entire `telemetry` block. Include all required fields in the winning source rather than splitting the endpoint and provider across delivery methods. See [managed-settings delivery precedence](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#across-managed-settings-delivery-methods) and the [header provider reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference#dynamic-authentication-headers) for more information.
